nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability distribution on a type $\alpha$ and let $f, g, f', g'$ assign a game to each point. If $\Pr[f(a) = 1] + \Pr[g(a) = 1] = \Pr[f'(a) = 1] + \Pr[g'(a) = 1]$ for every $a$, then the same identity holds for the games obtained by first drawing $a \leftarrow \mu$.
nodes.title: Averaging a pointwise identity between sums of success probabilities

nodes.summary: A distribution on $\{0, 1\}$ whose support does not contain $\lnot b$ is the point mass at $b$.
nodes.title: A game that never outputs `¬ b` always outputs `b`

nodes.summary: For two values $m$ and $m'$, the distribution that picks $m$ or $m'$ according to a fair coin.
nodes.title: The two-point distribution

nodes.summary: If three families of games satisfy $\Pr[F(a) = 1] = \tfrac12 + \tfrac12 \bigl(\Pr[G(a) = 1] - \Pr[H(a) = 1]\bigr)$ for every $a$, the same identity holds for the games that first draw $a$ from a probability distribution $\mu$.
nodes.title: Averaging an affine identity

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a probability distribution on a type $\alpha$, let $F$ and $G$ assign a game (a distribution on $\{0, 1\}$) to each point, and let $\varepsilon \ge 0$. If $\Pr[F(x) = 1] \le \Pr[G(x) = 1] + \varepsilon$ for every $x$ in the support of $X$, then the games obtained by first drawing $x \leftarrow X$ satisfy the same bound: $\Pr[F(X) = 1] \le \Pr[G(X) = 1] + \varepsilon$.
nodes.title: Averaging a pointwise bound

nodes.summary: For a probability distribution $\mu$ on a type $\alpha$ and games $F(a)$, the game that first draws $a \leftarrow \mu$ succeeds with probability $\sum_a \mu(a) \Pr[F(a) = 1]$.
nodes.title: Success probability of an average

nodes.summary: For every assignment $F$ of a game to each message, drawing the message from the two-point distribution on $m$ and $m'$ gives success probability $\tfrac12 \bigl(\Pr[F(m) = 1] + \Pr[F(m') = 1]\bigr)$.
nodes.title: Averaging over the two-point distribution

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
